plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 15.4.5
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the extension of Green's Theorem to a multiply connected region with one hole. Panel (a): a blob-shaped region R with a hole; the outer boundary C1 is oriented counterclockwise and the inner boundary C2 surrounding the hole is oriented clockwise, illustrating the positive orientation convention for a multiply connected region. Panel (b): the same region with two horizontal cuts introduced, dividing R into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R''; arrows along the cuts show the opposing orientations (right-pointing on one side, left-pointing on the other) which cancel in the sum, while C1 and C2 retain their original orientations. The figure shows how introducing cuts reduces a multiply connected region to simply connected parts, allowing Green's Theorem to be applied to each piece separately and then combined to give the extended result.

interactionPlan.concept: Green's Theorem extends to a multiply connected region by cutting it into simply connected pieces: the cuts are traversed twice in opposite directions so their contributions cancel, leaving the outer boundary counterclockwise and the inner boundary clockwise.

interactions.teaches: The orientation convention is not tied to a particular shape: however the hole is moved or resized, the outer curve stays counterclockwise, the inner curve stays clockwise, and the cuts re-attach so the region is always on the left of the traversal.

demo_steps.title: A doubly connected region
demo_steps.narration: The shaded region R lies between an outer curve C₁ and the boundary C₂ of a hole. Because of the hole, R is not simply connected, so Green's Theorem does not apply directly.

demo_steps.title: Positive orientation means region on your left
demo_steps.narration: Walk the boundary: on C₁ you travel counterclockwise, but on C₂ you must travel clockwise. In both cases the shaded region stays on your left — that is the single rule behind the two apparently opposite directions.

demo_steps.title: Introduce two cuts
demo_steps.narration: Two horizontal cuts are drawn from the outer curve to the hole. Each cut is a single segment, but it will be traversed once in each direction.

demo_steps.title: Two simply connected pieces
demo_steps.narration: The cuts split R into an upper piece R′ and a lower piece R″. Each has no hole, so Green's Theorem applies to each separately; their boundaries include the cut segments.

demo_steps.title: The cuts cancel
demo_steps.narration: Along each cut, R′ is traversed rightward while R″ is traversed leftward. The two line integrals are negatives of each other and cancel, leaving exactly the integral over C₁ counterclockwise plus C₂ clockwise.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The 'backwards' clockwise orientation of the hole is forced by one rule — keep the region on your left — and the cuts that prove it disappear because every cut is walked once in each direction.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two stacked panels sharing the same blob. The blob is a smooth closed curve with a deep concave notch on its left side, filled pale sky blue with a thick medium-blue outline; inside it, a white kidney-shaped hole sits right of center with the same thick blue outline. Large chunky triangular blue arrowheads sit on the curves: on C₁ one near the top pointing left and one near the bottom-right pointing right (counterclockwise); on C₂ one on the upper right pointing up-right and ones on the lower left pointing up/left, giving clockwise traversal relative to the region. Labels are serif italic math type: C₁ above the blob, R (or R′/R″) inside the shading, C₂ just above the hole. Panel (b) adds two horizontal black cut bands, each a pair of closely spaced thin black lines connecting the outer curve to the hole — one band on the left running from the notch to the hole, one on the right running from the hole to the outer curve — with small black arrows: upper line of each band pointing right, lower line pointing left. Captions '(a)' and '(b)' centered below each panel. In the interactive version, the hole is a draggable/resizable shape and the cuts automatically re-anchor horizontally to the nearest outer-curve points; during the 'separate' state the upper and lower halves slide apart vertically by a small gap so R′ and R″ read as two distinct closed regions, and in the final state the cut arrows fade/strike through to show cancellation.

discrepancies: Panel layout differs: the source stacks (a) above (b); the generated figure places them side-by-side, changing the overall composition (still both panels present).
The hole boundary C₂ is drawn as a nearly round blob; the source hole has a pronounced kidney/bean concavity biting in from the left, which is a visually distinctive feature of the figure.
In panel (b) the R″ label sits outside the shaded region, below/overlapping the lower blue boundary curve, instead of inside the lower sub-region as in the source.
The outer curve's left-side notch is shallower/wider than the source's deep narrow indentation, and the hole is placed lower-right rather than centre-right relative to the blob.
Cut arrowheads and double-line cuts in (b) render much smaller/fainter relative to the figure than the bold black arrows in the source.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-conceived recreation of the multiply-connected-region figure with an excellent step-through demo, stage buttons, orientation walker and draggable/resizable hole; weakest points are the over-round hole shape, the side-by-side rather than stacked panels, and the R″ label sitting outside the region.

discrepancies: In the generated figure the hole sits noticeably further right and lower than in the source, leaving only a thin sliver of shaded region between C₂ and the right-hand part of C₁; the source keeps a comfortably wide band of R all around the hole.

The hole's 'bite' is exaggerated so the white interior reads as a small pinched shape rather than the source's plump kidney/bean; its three clockwise arrowheads therefore crowd each other and nearly touch the outer curve.
Labels R and C₂ are placed almost side-by-side in panel (a) (and R′/C₂ in panel (b)), whereas the source separates R high in the region and C₂ clearly above the hole.

The two horizontal cut pairs in panel (b) are much shorter and visually lighter than the bold black double lines with prominent arrowheads in the source; the left-hand cut in particular barely reads at inline size.

Extra annotation text ('positive orientation: region always on the left', 'cut contributions cancel in pairs') and orange walker markers appear on some steps; these do not exist in the source (acceptable as teaching aids but they change the look on those steps).
evaluation.notes: A recognizable, conceptually correct reproduction of the two-panel Green's Theorem multiply-connected figure with an unusually rich and well-wired interaction set (step player, cut stages, orientation walker, hole size/drag); the main weaknesses are the shrunken, right-shifted hole that thins the shaded band, crowded R/C₂ label pairs, and cuts that read weaker than the source's bold black lines.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); remaining issues are concrete rendering details—hole placement/size, label separation, and cut line weight—so the generator should refine execution.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Panel (b) cuts are far too short and cramped: in the source each cut is a long horizontal segment reaching from the outer curve C₁ across to the hole on both left and right, drawn as a clearly separated pair (rightward arrow above, leftward arrow below). In the render the black cut segments are tiny stubs hugging the hole with near-touching arrowheads, making the key construction hard to read.

The hole is proportionally smaller and rounder than the source's large kidney/bean-shaped hole with its deep left bite; consequently C₂'s characteristic shape and the visual balance between region and hole differ.

In the source the C₂ label sits outside the shaded region above the hole with clear white space; here it is placed over the shaded fill immediately above the hole, relying on a halo, and in panel (b) it crowds the top of the hole/cut area.
Hole boundary arrowheads are smaller/less prominent than the bold triangular arrowheads of the source, and only weakly convey the clockwise orientation of C₂ at a glance.

The source's lower cut arrows (leftward) appear on both left and right of the hole at a clearly distinct y-level; in the render the two levels (±9 px) are almost coincident at display scale, so the 'traversed twice in opposite directions' idea is visually lost at default size.
evaluation.notes: Colors, composition, two-panel stacking, and all key labels (C₁, C₂, R, R′, R″, (a), (b)) closely track the source and the step-player/stage/drag/slider interactions are genuinely pedagogical, but the cut segments in panel (b) render as cramped stubs with near-coincident levels and the hole is under-sized, weakening the figure's central construction.

discrepancies: Panel (b) cuts are far too short and cramped: in the source each cut is a long horizontal segment reaching from the outer curve C₁ across to the hole on both left and right, drawn as a clearly separated pair (rightward arrow above, leftward arrow below). In the render the black cut segments are tiny stubs hugging the hole with near-touching arrowheads, making the key construction hard to read.

The hole is proportionally smaller and rounder than the source's large kidney/bean-shaped hole with its deep left bite; consequently C₂'s characteristic shape and the visual balance between region and hole differ.

In the source the C₂ label sits outside the shaded region above the hole with clear white space; here it is placed over the shaded fill immediately above the hole, relying on a halo, and in panel (b) it crowds the top of the hole/cut area.
Hole boundary arrowheads are smaller/less prominent than the bold triangular arrowheads of the source, and only weakly convey the clockwise orientation of C₂ at a glance.

The source's lower cut arrows (leftward) appear on both left and right of the hole at a clearly distinct y-level; in the render the two levels (±9 px) are almost coincident at display scale, so the 'traversed twice in opposite directions' idea is visually lost at default size.
claude-opus-5.notes: Colors, composition, two-panel stacking, and all key labels (C₁, C₂, R, R′, R″, (a), (b)) closely track the source and the step-player/stage/drag/slider interactions are genuinely pedagogical, but the cut segments in panel (b) render as cramped stubs with near-coincident levels and the hole is under-sized, weakening the figure's central construction.
